Async reminder deletions are fire-and-forget when cancelling a booking
deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async. They call Twilio or SendGrid and then update or delete the workflowReminder row. In the cancel handler they are called inside forEach without await. The old code deleted the DB rows through prisma promises that were included in Promise.all. The new code no longer awaits any of the reminder work. The handler then awaits sendCancelledEmails and returns. The DB deletes are only queued as lazy Prisma promises and are awaited after the loop, so none of them run. That failing reminder stays cancelled=true and is retried first on every run until its scheduledDate passes, and every reminder after it in the list is never cancelled.

Emails are sent for the unfiltered guest list, not the saved guests
Duplicate and blacklisted guests are filtered into uniqueGuests, and only uniqueGuests are saved. At the end, sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is called with the raw input, so newGuests includes the filtered-out addresses. Any filtered address that is already an attendee is matched in `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and gets the 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' email.
Existing attendees receive the wrong email (a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the guests-added notice). The email logic does not respect t

Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and the input is not deduped
The blacklist is lowercased, but each guest is compared as-is with includes(guest). 'Bad@Example.com' therefore bypasses a blacklist entry 'bad@example.com'. The same applies to the existing-attendee comparison. Duplicates within the input are also not removed on the server, since that check exists only in the client dialog, so a direct API call with the same email twice creates duplicate attendee rows.

Team admin/owner authorization requires both roles (&& instead of ||)
isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). The name and intent are "admin or owner", but the && means the user must pass both checks. Whether a team admin who is not an owner passes depends on how isTeamOwner is implemented, and a plain owner may fail isTeamAdmin if that checks only the ADMIN role. Such users are rejected with FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. The `?? 0` fallback also runs both team queries for bookings that have no team.

comment_verdicts.text:
Storage failures in Create and Update are recorded as legacy durations
When d.Storage.Create (line 45) or d.Storage.Update (line 129) fails, the code calls recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) rather than recordStorageDuration.
Storage errors are counted as legacy errors, so metrics and alerts are wrong.

Async legacy writes reuse the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns
Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection now run the legacy write in a goroutine. Each goroutine derives its context with context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) from the request ctx and returns without waiting. The request ctx is cancelled once the HTTP handler returns, so the derived context is cancelled with it. The 10s timeout therefore only matters if the request is still alive. The legacy call usually sees a cancelled context and fails, or never runs. The legacy store silently stops receiving writes

Delete uses the wrong logger and the wrong metric label
Delete builds the enriched logger `log` but then calls klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log), so the name, kind and method values are dropped from the context. On success it also passes `name` instead of options.Kind as the kind label to recordStorageDuration.
Metric label cardinality grows with object names, and logs downstream of Delete lack context.

DeleteCollection records legacy duration with the storage metric
In the legacy goroutine of DeleteCollection, the result of Legacy.DeleteCollection is reported via recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration.
Storage metrics are polluted by legacy timings and errors, and legacy delete-collection metrics are never emitted.

judge_pairs.reason: Storage failure in Create/Update wrongly recorded with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration.
Delete uses d.Log instead of enriched log variable in klog.NewContext.
Delete passes name instead of options.Kind as metrics kind label.
